original: A neural controller acts through the mechanics to which it is connected.
original_full_line: A neural controller acts through the mechanics to which it is connected. Changing muscle attachments, joint motion, inertia, or actuator behavior changes the mechanical response to a command and the sensory signals returned to the circuit. A controller that produces alternating motor activity can therefore fail to coordinate loading when transferred to a different body. Investigating that transfer requires tools that make the mechanical assumptions, neural computations, and exchanged signals accessible to inspection and controlled testing.
proposed_change: Describe neural and mechanical models, actuator commands, and returning sensory measurements before the Li/Deng transfer. Credit the course project to Morrow and Bolen and the passive toe change to Bolen.
rationale: The failure on ground contact matters once the reader understands what was connected and why a command can have a different mechanical consequence.
related_theme: context, credit; related to AD-T1, AD-C1, AD-C2

original: The developed capabilities serve different parts of one experiment
original_full_line: The developed capabilities serve different parts of one experiment (Table~\ref{tab:sns_capability}). Graphical tools support circuit construction and inspection. Headless execution runs a configured experiment without opening its graphical interface, allowing repeated trials and parameter searches. Saved model identities, parameters, and recordings connect these forms of work. A universal graphical application orchestrating every preparation and calibration operation remains a proposed extension; the reported evidence concerns the implemented components and named workflows.
proposed_change: Pair each authored block, adaptation, interface, or driver with its upstream source, user action, and actual test in the contribution table. Retain the division between CAD assembly, OpenSim conversion, and the runtime bridge.
rationale: The inventory names software categories without identifying the component a researcher opens or the result it produced. The bridge is an especially easy place to confuse model conversion and signal exchange.
related_theme: function, interface; related to AD-T2, AD-T3

original: Their offline MN-output fits could satisfy an activation-error criterion without reproducing the intended PF timing.
original_full_line: Intermediate verification exposed a different limitation in the s3k and syn6 human-model controllers. Their offline MN-output fits could satisfy an activation-error criterion without reproducing the intended PF timing. In syn6, none of twelve channels passed the combined provisional timing checks. Actual PF activity required three components per side to explain \qty{99}{\percent} of centered variance, compared with six for the intended primitives, and one channel remained active throughout the cycle. The corresponding s3k activity required two components per side, while quantitative intended PF windows had not been declared. These are descriptions of the measured signals, not minimum neuron counts.
proposed_change: Organize this result around one mechanism. Good motor-output fits concealed incorrect PF timing, prescribed replay improved timing, and the subsequent live mechanical loop still failed the joint and/or rhythm criteria.
rationale: The three results test different properties. Twelve cycle-averaged channel checks and 48 later channel-cycle checks have different criteria and denominators.

original: establish coupled balance and locomotor behaviors
original_full_line: The later virtual-harness-assisted evaluations establish coupled balance and locomotor behaviors while retaining their stated support conditions. In the human-model experiment, stepping persists after the supplementary left/right hand-drive channels are removed, in place under the support rig; the shared locomotor-drive input remains active. In the separate robot-model experiment, the robot model progresses under its harness with reduced drive (Section~\ref{sec:sns_controller_comparison}). Neural-drive dependence and mechanical-support dependence are different experimental questions. The balance-platform studies provide a separate hardware precedent for BPA-actuated balance with pseudo-vestibular feedback \citep{bolen_balance_2024,bolen_selfbalancing_2024,bolen_selfbalancing_srs_2024}.
proposed_change: Describe human stepping in place under support with the shared drive retained and the separate supported robot progression. Name the physical balance-platform work only as its own hardware experiment.
rationale: Suspended/assisted stepping and low supplementary drive cannot establish independent balance or unsupported gait. Chapter D retains the shared human command at 2.0773 nA.

original: A separate W2L bilateral-RG+Ib-port neural-core benchmark
original_full_line: Removing nominal constant weight support did not remove the position-control harness: its mean vertical force still supplied approximately \qty{16.75}{\percent}, using the legacy \qty{411}{\newton} weight denominator over \qtyrange{4.5}{30}{\second}. Contact duty remained below the strict walking criterion. These trials demonstrate repeatable stepping with that remaining assistance. A separate W2L bilateral-RG+Ib-port neural-core benchmark measured a 1.425 ratio for one block of 10,000 warm updates per backend, following 5,000 parity steps. Its saved \qty{30}{\second} body trajectories also agreed exactly. The isolated neural-update ratio does not measure acceleration of the complete neuromechanical simulation.
proposed_change: Move the W2L warm-neural-update result from the mechanical-assistance paragraph to computational performance; name its warm update count and matching check. Give the distinct workload for each timing row.
rationale: A neural-kernel timing cannot explain the amount of vertical support in a walking experiment. It cannot substitute for a complete-process time.

original: Full records preserve configuration, source hashes, compiled model, actual input samples, and aligned neural/mechanical states.
original_full_line: Table~\ref{tab:app_script_map} identifies the executable sources supporting the chapter's tests. Full records preserve configuration, source hashes, compiled model, actual input samples, and aligned neural/mechanical states. A figure can summarize an experiment, but cannot replace those records. Reproduction should use the recorded configuration and environment, then compare arrays before adding a new intervention. Unavailable external raw recordings are identified in the handoff rather than reconstructed from a picture.
proposed_change: Restrict the statement to experiments whose input arrays were retained. Keep the reported absence of the original BiW2Lvar+ launch adapter and complete command stream.
rationale: The retained adapter changes sustained commands as well as afferent return. D 192 explicitly says the original inputs were not fully captured; a blanket reproducibility claim contradicts the evidence.

original: The native baseline and rejected adaptation are distinct results
original_full_line: The custom SCONE runtime for the model of \citet{dirusso_investigating_2023} was subsequently built, and a \qty{10}{\second} replay in the original mechanical model reproduced the native baseline, including an exact saved fresh-process repeat. This verifies execution of that reference stack; it does not validate transfer to Gait2392 or establish physiological validity. An exploratory adaptation reproduced its corrected Python equations in a compiled implementation within $3.34\times10^{-16}$ over 2000 steps. Nevertheless, its 960-trial duration-and-speed search selected a tumbling trajectory, which was rejected as walking. Equation agreement did not establish transfer of the source controller's locomotion. The native baseline and rejected adaptation are distinct results: reproducing the original stack supplies a reference for transfer, while the unsuccessful search remains rejected as walking.
also: D 353, plus the chapter's model comparison
proposed_change: State once that the native SCONE baseline was subsequently reproduced, then distinguish the rejected Gait2392 adaptation and its tumbling trajectory.
rationale: The failed transfer is informative. Recapping the distinction twice in the same paragraph obscures chronology and makes an adaptation sound like a new successful reproduction.

original_full_line: is the bend signal handed to the force model. Each family's turn angle $\alpha_{f}$ ramps with knee angle between the two route-state events that bound it, holding zero before the first event and its plateau after the second, so the topology state and the bending signal are two readings of one record. The formulation is joint-agnostic: it requires only a fixed route representation with one crossing segment, per-angle transforms between the two body frames, and clearance envelopes on each side, so it carries unchanged to the other wrapped routes of this program.
proposed_change: State the one-crossing, sagittal-plane geometry and monotonic sweep. Describe the reverse activation pose as inferred from that recorded active set. Identify R times turning angle as an arc length, and identify which angle-wrapping error atan2 avoids.
rationale: A forward grid sweep does not independently establish reverse contact hysteresis or general three-dimensional topology. The arc-length product has units of length; the signed atan2 result still has its standard branch cut.

Source availability should be checked during curation; records whose sources cannot be located should be removed from the working research base rather than treated as verified evidence.
